title: Microscopy image realism does not ensure preservation of cell-population phenotypes
summary: Experiments on LIVECell found that microscopy images judged realistic at the image level can still fail to preserve population-level cellular phenotypes. The paper evaluates generated images across multiple representations, showing that conventional visual-fidelity measures alone do not establish biological congruence. The result is limited to the dataset and generation methods studied.
ai_technology: Generative microscopy models assessed using biological-congruence measures
organization: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI), Kaiserslautern; RPTU Kaiserslautern-Landau

evidence.tested: Generated LIVECell images were assessed for image-level fidelity and population-level phenotype preservation; the measures could disagree.
evidence.unknown: The result is bounded to the LIVECell data and generation methods evaluated.
evidence.ai_role: Generative models create synthetic microscopy images; representation-based measures assess whether they preserve biological phenotypes.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
